_comment: Port-forwarding guides used by porch connect manual (lib/porch_setup/net/router.py). Brands are matched in order: ISP gateways first. Menu paths are typical; firmware varies.

brands.name: Xfinity / Comcast gateway
brands.admin_url: Xfinity app (the 10.0.0.1 page mostly redirects there)
brands.menu: Xfinity app > WiFi > View WiFi equipment > Advanced settings > Port forwarding > Add port forward
brands.notes: Pick this box from the device list, then add each port. If xFi Advanced Security is on it can block inbound traffic; turn it off or allow this device. If you run your own router behind the gateway, either put the gateway in bridge mode or forward on both (double NAT).

brands.name: AT&T gateway (BGW210 / BGW320 / Pace / Arris)
brands.menu: Firewall > NAT/Gaming > Custom Services (create one per port) > Needed by Device: this box
brands.notes: Changes ask for the Device Access Code printed on the gateway's sticker. With your own router behind it, use IP Passthrough instead of forwarding twice.

brands.name: Verizon Fios router (G3100 / CR1000A)
brands.menu: Advanced > Security & Firewall > Port Forwarding
brands.notes: The admin password is on the router's sticker. The My Fios app also has Port Forwarding under Internet > My Network > Advanced.

brands.name: Spectrum router
brands.menu: My Spectrum app > Services > Internet > your router > Advanced Settings > Port Forwarding > Add Port Forward
brands.notes: Spectrum's own routers (Askey/Sagemcom/Wave 2) are managed from the app.

brands.name: Cox Panoramic Wifi
brands.menu: Connect > See Network > Advanced Settings > Port Forwarding > Add Port Forward

brands.name: CenturyLink / Quantum Fiber modem
brands.menu: Advanced Setup > Port Forwarding (Quantum Fiber: the Quantum Fiber app > Network > Port Forwarding)
brands.notes: The admin login is on the modem's sticker.

brands.name: Frontier router
brands.menu: Advanced > Security & Firewall > Port Forwarding (Fios-style menus) or Firewall > Port Forwarding

brands.name: Starlink
brands.menu: Not possible on residential plans
brands.notes: Starlink residential service is behind carrier-grade NAT, so port forwarding cannot work, even with your own router in bypass mode. Use a relay mode (or IPv6-only, with its caveat).

brands.name: T-Mobile Home Internet
brands.menu: Not possible
brands.notes: T-Mobile Home Internet is behind carrier-grade NAT; port forwarding cannot work. Use a relay mode.

brands.name: eero
brands.menu: eero app > Settings > Network settings > Reservations & port forwarding > Add a reservation (this box) > Add port forward
brands.notes: Reserve this box's IP first, then add the port forwards on that reservation.
brands.upnp: eero app > Settings > Network settings > UPnP

brands.name: Google Nest Wifi / Google Wifi
brands.menu: Google Home app > Wi-Fi > Settings > Advanced networking > Port management > + (pick this box) > add each port
brands.upnp: Google Home app > Wi-Fi > Settings > Advanced networking > UPnP

brands.name: TP-Link Deco
brands.menu: Deco app > More > Advanced > NAT Forwarding > Port Forwarding > +
brands.upnp: Deco app > More > Advanced > NAT Forwarding > UPnP

brands.name: NETGEAR (Nighthawk / Orbi)
brands.menu: Advanced > Advanced Setup > Port Forwarding / Port Triggering > Port Forwarding > + Add (Orbi: Advanced > Advanced Setup > Port Forwarding)
brands.notes: Choose 'Add Custom Service', TCP, the same external and internal port, and this box's IP. Also reserve the IP under Advanced > Setup > LAN Setup > Address Reservation.
brands.upnp: Advanced > Advanced Setup > UPnP > Turn UPnP On

brands.name: TP-Link
brands.menu: Advanced > NAT Forwarding > Virtual Servers (or Port Forwarding) > Add
brands.notes: Older firmware calls it Forwarding > Virtual Servers.

brands.name: ASUS
brands.menu: Advanced Settings > WAN > Virtual Server / Port Forwarding > Add profile
brands.notes: Turn on 'Enable Port Forwarding' at the top of the page.
brands.upnp: Advanced Settings > WAN > Internet Connection > Enable UPnP

brands.name: Linksys
brands.menu: Security > Apps and Gaming > Single Port Forwarding (Velop: the Linksys app > Advanced settings > Port forwarding)

brands.name: Ubiquiti UniFi / EdgeRouter
brands.admin_url: UniFi Network (https://unifi.ui.com or the console's IP)
brands.menu: UniFi: Settings > Firewall & Security > Port Forwarding > Create Entry (older: Settings > Routing & Firewall > Port Forwarding). EdgeRouter: Firewall/NAT > Port Forwarding

brands.name: AVM FRITZ!Box
brands.menu: Internet > Permit Access > Port Sharing > Add Device for Sharing > this box > New Sharing > Port sharing
brands.upnp: Same page: 'Permit independent port sharing for this device'

brands.name: MikroTik
brands.menu: IP > Firewall > NAT > + : chain=dstnat, protocol=tcp, dst-port=<port>, in-interface=<WAN>, action=dst-nat, to-addresses=<this box>
brands.notes: Make sure the filter rules accept the forwarded traffic (the default config's 'drop all not DSTNATed' rule allows it).
brands.upnp: IP > UPnP (enable, mark the WAN interface external)

brands.name: D-Link
brands.menu: Advanced > Port Forwarding (older: Advanced > Virtual Server)

brands.name: Belkin
brands.menu: Firewall > Virtual Servers

brands.name: Synology router (SRM)
brands.menu: Network Center > Port Forwarding > Create

brands.name: Huawei
brands.menu: More Functions > Security Settings > NAT Service / Port Mapping
brands.notes: Huawei 4G/5G routers on mobile networks are usually behind carrier-grade NAT; forwarding will not help there.

brands.name: ZTE
brands.menu: Internet > Security > Port Forwarding (or Advanced > NAT > Port Forwarding)
brands.notes: ZTE 4G/5G routers on mobile networks are usually behind carrier-grade NAT.

brands.name: Tenda
brands.menu: Advanced > Port Forwarding (older: Advanced > Virtual Server)

brands.name: Zyxel
brands.menu: Network Setting > NAT > Port Forwarding > Add New Rule

brands.name: Xiaomi
brands.menu: Advanced settings > Port forwarding > Add rule

brands.name: OpenWrt
brands.menu: Network > Firewall > Port Forwards > Add

brands.name: pfSense / OPNsense
brands.menu: Firewall > NAT > Port Forward > Add (OPNsense newer: Firewall > NAT > Destination NAT)
brands.notes: Keep 'Filter rule association' so the matching pass rule is created.

brands.name: ARRIS / SURFboard
brands.menu: Advanced > Firewall > Port Forwarding (SURFboard mAX: SURFboard Central app > My Network > Port Management)
brands.notes: A SURFboard cable modem without Wi-Fi has no router: forward on the router plugged into it.

brands.name: Technicolor (ISP gateway)
brands.menu: Advanced > Port Forwarding (ISP firmware varies)

brands.name: Sagemcom (ISP gateway)
brands.menu: Access Control > Port Forwarding (ISP firmware varies)

brands.name: Motorola
brands.menu: Advanced > Forwarding

brands.name: Apple AirPort
brands.menu: AirPort Utility > (base station) > Edit > Network > Port Settings > +
brands.notes: AirPort base stations also speak NAT-PMP, so automatic mode may already work.

generic.name: your router
generic.menu: Look for 'Port Forwarding', 'Virtual Server', 'NAT' or 'Port Mapping', usually under Advanced, Firewall or Security.
generic.notes: The admin login is often on a sticker on the router. Forward each port to this box's LAN IP and give the box a DHCP reservation so its IP never changes.
